label: copy-phase echo of w as the 1st or 2nd copied token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input is the letter w and that input is the echo of original token 0 or 1 (recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. the first two steps after <DEL>). Magnitude: strong (~3-3.9, top quartiles) when w is the first original token being echoed right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, 81% of mass); weaker (~0.05-1.3) when w is original token 1 echoed at recall_idx 2. Does not fire on w in the original phase, on w at later copy positions (recall_idx >= 3), or on any other token (only stray tiny activations). Main false positives are weak recall_idx-2 cases that fall to zero.

issues: Most claims hold. All activation mass is in the copy phase and 100% of mass is on in_tok w. recall_idx 1 holds 81.2% of mass and 2 holds 18.8%, with only 8 stray steps at recall_idx 3. recall_idx==1 & w has precision 1.0.

The false positives are not scattered noise. They are a systematic length effect at recall_idx 2. With w at recall_idx 2, dev precision is 0.056 for L=3 (468 predicted, almost none active) and 0.646 for L=4 (2362 predicted). For L=5..9 it is 1.0. The 'w echoed as the 2nd copied token' case fails when that echo comes at the last or second-to-last copy step (to_go = L-3 is 0 or 1). The explanation's 'most false positives are weak recall_idx 2 cases where the activation drops to zero' misses that they are tied to L=3/4.
The label 'as the 1st or 2nd copied token' overclaims for short sequences: at L=3 the second-position w case essentially never fires.
Partial structure inside L=4: precision rises to 0.92 when w occurs 2+ times in the original (in_count>=2). This is not fully resolved.
Test misses on the original predicate: 28 missed steps holding 0.0% of mass. Coverage is fine.

Excluding L=3 gives test F1 0.985 vs 0.980 for the original predicate. Requiring L>=5 for recall_idx 2 gives precision 0.99997 but F1 0.974. So the headline numbers barely change, but the stated predicate includes a systematic counterexample class.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase echo of w as the 1st copied token (strong), or the 2nd copied token (weak) except in very short sequences (L=3 never, L=4 partially)

final_label: copy-phase echo of w as the 1st copied token (strong), or the 2nd copied token (weak) except in very short sequences (L=3 never, L=4 partially)
